fidelitymem-adaptive-hybrid-memory.repositoryDescription: FidelityMem: Recall-Constrained Adaptive Hybrid Memory for LLM Agents
fidelitymem-adaptive-hybrid-memory.overview: Module Role --- --- window.py Adaptive working window: per-message retention score, boundary triggers (token pressure, topic shift, task completion, inactivity), eviction into extraction. extraction.py Candidate memories with types (semantic / episodic / procedural / relational), entities, numbers, dates, negations, relations. validation.py Stage 1 source & consistency (trust, contradiction, supersede-not-delete, untrusted-instruction guard). Stage 2 relevance & utility (durability score, fact-aware dedupe). compression.py Four-level compression ladder and the fidelity gate : probes built from the raw source must survive, or the level backs off. Stage 3. stores/ Immutable archival store (JSONL-persistable), BM25, dense index with a hermetic hashing embedder, relation graph with relation-following expansion and hub penalty, trie for exact/prefix identifiers. retrieval/ Query classification, per-type plans, RRF fusion + ranking function, relation chaining for multi-hop, sufficiency check and raw-source expansion, token-budgeted context. controller.py Recall-constrained policy search over (compression level, top-k, expansion budget, routes) with tuning/hold-out split, promotion, rejec
features: needs ANTHROPIC API KEY (or ANTHROPIC AUTH TOKEN / ant auth login )

heart-disease-prediction-using-generativ.overview: Heart-risk estimate + personalised next steps from a hybrid content / collaborative recommender.
features: Risk model — predicts a heart-disease risk score from 11 clinical inputs. Candidates (each in one sklearn Pipeline , imputation fitted inside CV folds): logistic regression, gradient boosting and a PyTorch MLP .
Hybrid recommender — ranks 13 lifestyle / screening / clinical interventions:
Content-based: patient needs (lipids, BP, glucose, fitness, metabolic, cardiac work-up) matched to each intervention's target vector.

Collaborative: a PyTorch two-tower model. The patient tower is an MLP on features plus the mean embedding of interventions the patient already liked; the item tower is an id embedding plus content features. It handles cold start (features only) and warm start (liked items).
Hybrid: α·content + (1-α)·collaborative , with α tuned on a validation split. A safety rule always surfaces a cardiology referral at high scores.
Education links from the NIH/NLM MedlinePlus web service (free, no key).
MLflow experiment tracking and model registry, browsable from the app's 🧪 MLflow tab.

natural-disaster-prediction-and-manageme.repositoryDescription: Natural disaster prediction using deep learning and machine learning (VIT University)
natural-disaster-prediction-and-manageme.overview: Estimates, live data and alerting for earthquakes, tsunamis, floods, hurricanes and storms. Started as a VIT University capstone in 2020 (Flask 1, TensorFlow 1) and rebuilt in 2026 on FastAPI, scikit-learn, HTMX, Tailwind and Leaflet, with live feeds and a Claude-powered assistant. Outputs are statistical estimates and other organisations' live data. They are not operational forecasts or warnings. Earthquakes cannot be predicted: the earthquake page reports a historical hazard rate, and real-time alerts come from the USGS feed, not from a model.
features: Home: A live 3D globe of this week's USGS earthquakes, with module cards
Earthquake: Historical hazard for any place (rate and probability of M 6, 7, 8), the live USGS map, the week's strongest real earthquakes with one-click "Nearby help"
Flood: River level 1, 3 and 6 hours ahead for one gauge, shown next to "no change"
Tsunami, Hurricane, Storm: Small models with their held-out skill shown on the page
Live: GDACS global alerts, a weather outlook for any place, and the real-event alert watcher
Assistant: Plain-language questions answered with live tools and cited guidance (Claude key needed)
Alerts: Hospitals and police near a place or epicentre, then alert your contacts by email or SMS, optionally in other languages
natural-disaster-prediction-and-manageme.architecture: This is the short map. Detail lives in code-walkthrough.md (backend), frontend.md (browser side), models.md (every model) and statistics.md (generated numbers). A FastAPI application that renders server-side Jinja2 pages, enhanced with HTMX. Models are trained once from the command line and loaded from disk at request time. Nothing trains, downloads or writes files inside a web request.
